statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = n + max(0, n - 8) + max(0, n - 16) + max(0, n - 24).
preconditions: Let n = len(word). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 26; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 97 <= word[i] <= 122 (word[i] is a lowercase English letter); and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, word[i] != word[j].

statement: The function returns a result (it does not fail) for every word satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(word). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 26; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 97 <= word[i] <= 122; and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, word[i] != word[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= n.
preconditions: Let n = len(word). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 26; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 97 <= word[i] <= 122; and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, word[i] != word[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= 56.
preconditions: Let n = len(word). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 26; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 97 <= word[i] <= 122; and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, word[i] != word[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns r1 on word1 and r2 on word2, if n1 = n2 then r1 = r2.
preconditions: Let n1 = len(word1) and n2 = len(word2). Both word1 and word2 satisfy: 1 <= n1, n2 <= 26; all their bytes are lowercase English letters (97..122); and all letters within each word are distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns r1 on word1 and r2 on word2, if n1 <= n2 then r1 <= r2.
preconditions: Let n1 = len(word1) and n2 = len(word2). Both word1 and word2 satisfy: 1 <= n1, n2 <= 26; all their bytes are lowercase English letters (97..122); and all letters within each word are distinct.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every valid remapping of the n letters of word onto keys 2 through 9 and every ordering of the letters assigned to each key, the total number of pushes is at least r, where the push count of a letter is its 1-based position in the ordering of its assigned key and the total is the sum of these counts over all n letters.
preconditions: Let n = len(word). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 26; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 97 <= word[i] <= 122; and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, word[i] != word[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a valid remapping of the n letters of word onto keys 2 through 9 and an ordering of the letters assigned to each key such that the total number of pushes is exactly r and every key is assigned at most 4 letters.
preconditions: Let n = len(word). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 26; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 97 <= word[i] <= 122; and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, word[i] != word[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns r1 on word1 and r2 on word2, r2 - r1 = 1 + [n >= 8] + [n >= 16] + [n >= 24], where [P] is 1 when P is true and 0 otherwise.
preconditions: Let n1 = len(word1) and n2 = len(word2). Both word1 and word2 satisfy: 1 <= n1, n2 <= 26; all their bytes are lowercase English letters (97..122); and all letters within each word are distinct. Also n2 = n1 + 1, and let n = n1.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every remapping whose total number of pushes is r uses all eight keys; exactly two keys are assigned 4 letters and the other six keys are assigned 3 letters.
preconditions: Let n = len(word). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 26; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 97 <= word[i] <= 122; for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, word[i] != word[j]; and n = 26.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a remapping whose total number of pushes is r and in which each of the n letters is assigned to a different key, so every letter has push count 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(word). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 26; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 97 <= word[i] <= 122; for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, word[i] != word[j]; and n <= 8.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = n if and only if n <= 8.
preconditions: Let n = len(word). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 26; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 97 <= word[i] <= 122; and for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < n, word[i] != word[j].
